evaluations.label: A
errors: Says the space is for 'approximately 15 to 18 people'; the transcript says 15 people and 18 positions (16 if a two-person room becomes the reading room).

Says sharing offices with assistants is 'common in other faculties but not necessarily here'; Susan said the opposite: in every other faculty professors have their own office, and sharing with assistants is the school's implicit tradition.
Action Items section says '(none)', yet the transcript has clear assignments (Andre to check room separation, Susan to ask Maggie and Pierrette, everyone to bring preferences or a sketch).
Refers only to anonymous 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' for most statements, and 'Speaker 3, Speaker 1, Speaker 2, and Speaker 4 debated' gives no usable attribution.
Frames the lounge as a 'significant requirement' to serve as a meeting or overflow space; the transcript shows its purpose is an open question and Susan questioned whether it is needed.
strengths: Captures the main open questions (room splitting, four places in a three-person room, lounge purpose, Gisela).
Correctly notes the next meeting Tuesday at 2:00 PM and the other group working in parallel.
weaknesses: No action items and no owners at all, so someone who missed the meeting does not know who does what.
Speaker numbers instead of names make it hard to act on.
Misses the 16-slot arithmetic, the zero-growth point, the idea of placing Gisela with the school admin, and the Maggie and Pierrette follow-up as a named task by Susan.
Reverses the point about other faculties.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Minor: several timestamps are approximate (for example the 15 people / 18 positions point is stamped 04:00 and the Susan/Martin sharing point 14:33), but the content of each claim is supported.
Minor: says Susan 'wanted' the lounge to accommodate visitors; she said it should also serve as an overflow place, after first questioning whether it was needed.
strengths: Most accurate of the four: names, numbers (15 people, 18 positions, 16 with a two-person reading room, zero growth), and attributions all check out.
Action items carry correct owners: Andrei on room separation and authorization, Susan on asking Maggie and Pierrette.
Clearly states what was left unresolved (layout, lounge purpose, Gisela) and that the meeting was for gathering constraints.
Includes the smoking point and the fixed room count versus open assignments.
weaknesses: Action items list only two; it omits Andre's checks on fitting four desks in a three-person room and on placing Gisela with the other school admin.
The request that each person bring preferences and a sketch is in the body but not in the action list.
Leaves out the coffee/vending machine and cafeteria discussion and the MDM-meeting reason for an afternoon slot.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Action item assigns Andrei to 'follow up with absent team members (Maggie, Pierrette)'; Susan was the one who said she would ask them.
Calls the lounge a 'key' priority and says 'management recognizes this as a priority'; the transcript shows its purpose and even its need were questioned and left open.

Says the follow-up meeting was set 'to avoid conflicts with other morning commitments' and 'allows time for everyone to gather input'; the stated reason was the MDM meeting Tuesday morning, and the framing is partly embellished.
Says the team 'considers the current move a partial solution' and that 'management' has views; these are interpretations, not stated in the transcript.
Says project grouping is 'less important than proximity to meeting rooms and shared spaces'; nobody framed it that way, the point was that meeting rooms serve project collaboration.
Attributes 'distribute documents' as an Andre action item, which was a passing remark during the meeting, not a follow-up task.
Timestamps frequently do not match where the content appears.
strengths: Most comprehensive: covers four-desk squeeze, Gisela options including the school admin idea, coffee and vending machines, smoking, whiteboards, equipment.
Action items section includes the sketch/proposal request, the Tuesday afternoon meeting, and Andre's investigations.
Notes the other group and the plan to merge proposals.
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive (the same points on room splitting, growth and visitors appear in three or four sections), which hurts readability.
Contains several inflated or interpretive statements that are not in the transcript.
Misses Susan as the owner of the Maggie/Pierrette task.
Lumps everything under vague owners like 'meeting organizer'.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Says 'strong support for a dedicated lounge' and 'majority lean toward a mixed-use room'; the transcript shows Susan questioned the need and the use was left as an open discussion with no decision.
Next-step items have no named owners (Susan is the one to ask Maggie and Pierrette; Andre does the checks).
strengths: Accurate figures and facts: 15 people, about 18 positions, 16 with a two-person reading room, zero growth, vending machines on floors 1 and 3, cafeteria closes at 5, MDM meeting Tuesday morning.

Next Steps list is complete and specific: room separation and authorization, four desks in a three-person room, Gisela with the other school admin, Maggie and Pierrette's preferences, each attendee brings a sketch, follow-up Tuesday around 2 PM.
Good structure: space overview, constraints per person (Susan, Martin, Gisela), lounge debate, next steps; concise and scannable.
Captures nuance on Gisela (give her a one-person room if a professor volunteers to share, or a two-person room with a visitor slot) and that the lounge furnishing is a separate topic.
weaknesses: Slightly overstates consensus on the lounge.

rationale: D is the most useful: accurate, compact, and its next-steps list captures every follow-up (room separation, four desks in a three-person room, Gisela with the school admin, Maggie and Pierrette, bring a sketch, Tuesday at 2 PM), though without owners and with a slightly overstated lounge consensus. B is the most accurate and gives correct owners, but lists only two action items and omits several follow-ups. C is the most exhaustive but is long and repetitive, and it contains errors and embellishments, most notably assigning the Maggie/Pierrette follow-up to Andre instead of Susan and treating the lounge as a settled priority. A is weakest: it has no action items, uses anonymous speaker numbers, gives '15 to 18 people', and reverses the point about other faculties.
